rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer: Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the Apollo 11 landing [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". Columbia was part of the command and service module, which was built by North American Aviation [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". North American Aviation was the prime contractor for that module [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The heaters ran for about eight hours. Before launch, Oxygen tank No. 2 was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)".

The investigating board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)". The fault lay in the tank's thermostatic switches. Those switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC, and the heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts, but the switches were not changed [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". The board's report also called the switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)".

The Gemini flight he commanded was Gemini 8, in 1966, and it was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
Charlie Duke is the astronaut who caught German measles. His exposure started the crew swap ([[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"; [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)").

The swap brought in Jack Swigert, who became Apollo 13 command module pilot in place of Ken Mattingly ([[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Apollo 13 role is prime command module pilot (was backup command module pilot, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)").

Swigert later won election to the US House of Representatives, but he died before taking office ([[jack-swigert]] "[stated] Was elected to the US House of Representatives in 1982 but died before taking office (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)").

The notes do not give the cause or date of his death, or the district he was elected for.

rows.question: The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was carried by a spacecraft. Which Apollo 11 crew member piloted that kind of spacecraft, and what did he do during the landing?
rows.answer:
The tank that crippled Apollo 13 was oxygen tank No. 2. Its note describes it as an "Apollo 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion" [[oxygen-tank-2]] description: Apollo [unverified] 13 service module tank whose 28-volt thermostatic switches failed under 65-volt power and caused the explosion.

That tank was carried by the command and service module. [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Its service module carried the oxygen tanks that supplied power and air (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

The command and service module was piloted on Apollo 11 by Michael Collins, the command module pilot. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Command module pilot of Apollo 11 (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The note links him to the command and service module as its pilot, but I did not find that link stated as a fact line.

During the landing, Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The lunar module Eagle, not Collins, made the landing at the Sea of Tranquility. [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Lunar module Eagle landed on 1969-07-20 in the Sea of Tranquility (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: What was the improvised "mailbox" on Apollo 13 made from, and how did the crew build it?
rows.answer:
The "mailbox" was an improvised CO2 scrubber adapter made from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] Engineers devised an adapter from hoses, cardboard, plastic bags and tape (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

It was needed because the command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The command module's lithium hydroxide canisters were square and the lunar module's were round (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The crew built it from radioed instructions. [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] "[stated] The crew built it from radioed instructions (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The notes I opened do not give the build steps, the timing, or who wrote the instructions beyond a link from [[co2-scrubber-adapter]] to [[mission-control-houston]], which names it as the designer.

rows.question: List every Apollo mission in the brain that launched with a crew, with its launch date.
rows.answer:
Four Apollo missions in the brain launched with a crew:

- **Apollo 8**: launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders. [[apollo-8]] "[stated] Launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Apollo 1 is excluded. Its crew of Grissom, White and Chaffee died in a cabin fire during a launch rehearsal, so the mission never launched. rows.question: Which companies and laboratories built Apollo hardware in the brain, and what did each build?
rows.answer:
Four companies or laboratories in the brain built Apollo hardware:

- **Grumman** built the Apollo lunar module. [[grumman]] "[stated] Built the Apollo lunar module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The lunar module note agrees: [[lunar-module]] "[stated] Two-stage lander built by Grumman (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

- **North American Aviation** was the prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module. [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". The command and service module note agrees: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

- **Beech Aircraft** built the service module oxygen tanks, under North American Aviation. [[beech-aircraft]] "[stated] Built the service module oxygen tanks under North American Aviation (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". The tank note confirms the tank was built by Beech: [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)". That line describes the switches' specification, not the tank's maker, so the Beech build claim rests on the Beech Aircraft note alone.

- **MIT Instrumentation Laboratory**, led by Charles Stark Draper, designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system, including the Apollo guidance computer. [[mit-instrumentation-lab]] "[stated] Designed the Apollo guidance and navigation system (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-guidance-computer]] "[stated] Designed at the MIT Instrumentation Laboratory (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here is the answer again. The earlier citations left off the `[stated]` tag that starts each fact line, so I've copied each line in full.

1. **1970-04-06:** Blood tests from the physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

2. **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference. Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as command module pilot. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"

3. **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

4. **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded, about 56 hours into the flight. The mission goal changed from a lunar landing at Fra Mauro to a safe return to Earth, by a Mission Control abort decision. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

5. **1970-04-17:** The crew, using the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat, splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

6. **June 1970:** The Cortright board report was published. The board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)". [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)". The brain gives only the month for the report, not a day.
